KROWNLANDIA COMMUNITY LIBRARY · NOVEMBER 5, 2026

Krownlandia: Yet to build

A proposed development sequence for residents, guests and creators. This list separates the current prototype from future shared services and new platforms.

Already built: browser exploration, rides, lounges, homes, local rewards and keepsakes, progress backups, personal points-over-time, a calendar framework and photo/video capture.
Still future work: shared multiplayer presence, account-synchronized rewards, a public verified leaderboard, visitor activity auditing and a Unity version.

Next work queue · November 5 audit

This ordered queue takes precedence over the longer milestone descriptions below. Each item is a bounded deliverable, not a promised completion date. Ready means work can begin within current permissions; Decision needed means implementation waits for Lisa; Paused means do not resume automatically.

  1. Complete — Roadmap audit and working queue. Compared hosted version 249 with project notes, implementation and historical village descriptions. Preserved the historical inventory and separated future services from existing local features.
  2. Complete — Repeatable release check. One documented command now groups seven selected save, backup, rewards, gameplay/navigation and authorization suites. The optional built-artifact mode adds an eighth Worker/asset check after a fresh build. Failures and timeouts stop the run; output explicitly distinguishes deterministic checks from live browser verification. Riverbend practice pottery is now implemented.
  3. Complete — Riverbend practice pottery. The optional riverside workshop offers bowl/vase shaping, waves/dots decoration, finishing and restarting with native keyboard-operable controls. Inspired by PDF page 3; designs last only until page reload and do not change saved keepsakes, points or station eligibility. Live rendering and assistive-technology verification remain pending.
  4. Complete — Public source refresh. Reviewed and synchronized a sanitized snapshot of hosted version 252 on November 5. Private build records, credentials, account identifiers and registered hosting configuration remain excluded. No project-wide license has been selected. Shared identity and rewards architecture is the next design deliverable.
  5. Ready for design; Decision needed before activation — Shared identity and rewards. Write the server-data, ownership and migration proposal. Keep legacy browser points separate from verified scores; specify duplicate-claim protection. Present guest policy, retention and tracking decisions before enabling services.
  6. Ready for design; Decision needed before activation — Multiplayer pilot. Scope a two-visitor Town Square session, reconnect behavior, visibility/moderation controls, hosting requirements and acceptance checks. No paid service, visitor tracking or multiplayer deployment is authorized by this planning item.

Next historical expansion candidate: Meadowbrook weaving and market activity (PDF page 2). Existing Meadow homes are not the completed historical village. Leaderboards follow verified rewards; Unity begins as a separately scoped proof of concept.

Paused: the browser-review project, local-browser tooling, recurring visual checks and new sign-in attempts. Tester Viewer access and sign-in were verified November 5, but this cloud browser could not create a WebGL context. This is no longer an invitation blocker. Real 3D appearance, camera encoding and device performance remain unverified.

Decision needed: confirmed event details, Sunvale/Sunnyvale naming, asset usage rights and licensing, shared-account policy, public ranking privacy, moderation, retention and paid hosting. Existing calendar entries remain empty until confirmed; portal credits do not grant account permissions.

Run discipline: recover latest source, finish one useful deliverable, run relevant checks once after the final change, and update status with evidence. Publish changed Site content only after checks pass; do not deploy unchanged code or invent small features to fill a run. Skip blocked work for the next ready item and report the specific dependency.

Longer-term milestones

1. Test the visitor experience · Paused

Resume prerequisite: Lisa resumes the review project and a controllable WebGL-capable browser is available. Tester access is already verified. Then conduct an authorized walkthrough of entry/resume, navigation, seating, panel obstruction, day/night appearance and camera recording. Check desktop and small-screen controls, keyboard access and supported browsers.

Completion check: reproduce and prioritize findings, fix blocking issues, and record which real-browser behaviors were verified. Keep existing saves and backups intact.

2. Establish shared identity and services

Choose account identity, visitor display names and roles for guests, residents, place managers, administrators and agents. Decide what visitors can use without an account. Separate display credits such as “place manager” from actual permissions.

Design persistent server storage and an authenticated API with explicit ownership checks. Plan account recovery, data export, deletion and retention. Define which activities are logged and show visitors a clear notice before enabling tracking.

Completion check: two test accounts cannot access each other's private data, roles are enforced on the server, and recovery/export flows work.

3. Add server-verified rewards tracking

Keep the existing browser points as legacy local progress. Build a server-owned reward ledger recording account, station/activity, reward amount, server time and a unique claim identifier. Validate completion and eligibility on the server; make retries idempotent so repeated requests cannot award duplicate points.

Design reconciliation and backup migration deliberately: imported local scores must not become verified competitive scores merely because a client submits them. Preserve existing keepsakes and label historical, unverified totals clearly. Separate ordinary reward events from administrator adjustments and retain an audit trail for corrections.

Completion check: simultaneous claims, retries, offline/reconnect cases and manipulated client timestamps cannot duplicate or invent verified points.

4. Pilot multiplayer in one small area

Begin with a limited Town Square session where two invited test visitors can see each other's avatar and movement. Choose a real-time transport and hosting approach after testing latency, reconnect behavior, capacity and costs. Synchronize only the state needed for presence at first; keep the full park available as a single-player experience.

Define spawn points, session limits, disconnect cleanup, visibility choices and agent identification. Establish block/report and moderation behavior before adding chat or user-generated content. Decide separately whether seats, housing and activities are shared or instanced.

Completion check: visitors join, move, disconnect and reconnect predictably without losing local progress or gaining unauthorized control over another visitor.

5. Add leaderboards and useful administration

Once verified reward data exists, introduce opt-in hourly, daily, monthly, yearly and all-time rankings. Define Pacific-time boundaries, ties, privacy choices, corrections and anti-abuse rules. Keep legacy points separate from verified rankings.

Expand the current publication-only admin log to approved visitor/agent activity events. Show actor type, event, time and outcome with role-limited access. Avoid collecting chat, recordings or detailed movement by default; decide the minimum events needed and their retention.

Completion check: rankings derive from the server ledger, timezone boundaries and corrections are tested, and visitors can understand what is visible to others.

6. Build a Unity proof of concept

Start with one small scene - for example, the gate and Lisa's Coffee Shop - rather than attempting to convert the entire world at once. Choose target devices, rendering requirements and a supported Unity setup after reviewing current platform capabilities, terms and costs.

The current JavaScript/Three.js application is not already a Unity project. Plan to recreate or port scene geometry, materials, controls and interactions; review asset rights and performance. Maintain shared place IDs, reward definitions and documented save schemas.

Connect the Unity client to the same authenticated identity and reward services as the browser version. Neither client should be trusted to award points. Test control parity, seating, accessible UI, networking and save migration before expanding.

Completion check: a visitor completes one equivalent activity in each client, sees consistent verified progress, and can return to the browser version without losing data. A full Unity world, cross-play and VR remain later decisions.

7. Continue community-led world building

Review remaining original-document ideas against what is already built. Expand established villages only with verified source descriptions and credits. Confirm the Sunvale/Sunnyvale naming ambiguity before using it as a new village label. Publish actual events only after Lisa confirms their details.

Assess the living simulation and sticker artwork as separate integrations, including permissions and technical feasibility. Existing outbound links do not provide embedded simulation, shared accounts or imported emoji assets.

Unfinished improvements and verification work

  • Visitor onboarding: review first arrival, resume choices, finding help, map directions and rewards follow-through with a test visitor.
  • Visual finish: verify the cafe facade, counter, furniture, materials and night lighting in a real browser; inspect obstruction and legibility across the park.
  • Accessibility: test keyboard focus, screen-reader announcements, touch targets, narrow screens and reduced-motion behavior with actual browser/assistive technology.
  • Cameras: verify photo downloads, real codec support, video preview/playback and interruption recovery. Canvas captures exclude menus; use ordinary screenshots to review controls.
  • Performance: measure frame rate and memory on representative devices. Existing scene batching, distant-light limits and hidden-tab pauses are implemented, but measured GPU gains remain unverified.
  • Reliability: continue regression checks for saves, old backups, seated views, rides, stale controls and repeated actions; do not introduce new progress formats without migration tests.
  • GitHub: review and publish a sanitized source refresh beyond version 233, establish synchronization practice and decide licensing with rights holders.
  • Events: collect confirmed names, hosts, dates and destinations before populating the existing calendar; do not present simulated previews as live events.
  • Community integrations: inspect the living simulation and approved sticker assets when accessible; define permissions and integration scope before embedding or importing.

Maintaining this roadmap

Update these visitor documents with relevant published changes and keep the source snapshot explicit. Refresh all three reports at least monthly. Move an item to built only with implementation and verification evidence; use proposed, in progress, blocked and built states without inventing dates or contributor approvals. Keep the historical inventory separate from the people roster and obsolete social-contact list.

Working order and decisions

Recommended sequence: follow the ready queue above while visual review is paused. Shared identity/services precede verified rewards, multiplayer deployment and leaderboard/admin expansion; Unity remains a later proof of concept.

Lisa's decisions are needed for platform scope, guest/account policy, public ranking preferences, moderation, data retention, asset licensing and any paid hosting. This roadmap authorizes no purchase, tracking activation or permission change. No delivery dates or multiplayer capacity are promised.

Basis: current Krownlandia project notes and implementation through hosted version 249, the supplied historical PDF (pages 2-16), and Lisa's requested future multiplayer, rewards-tracking and Unity directions. Architecture and acceptance checks above are proposed next steps, not claims of completed features.

Prepared for Lisa Chandler. This document is a dated status and planning record; proposed work is not a promise of availability or delivery dates. Return to Krownlandia Gateway.
